subject: Coffee & Tea
title: Instant Coffee's Surprising Story
description: A 60-second lesson on Instant Coffee's Surprising Story.

hook.text: Instant coffee was invented in 1901 by a Japanese-American chemist named Satori Kato at a world's fair.

buildup.text: Nescafé launched in 1938 after Brazil asked Nestlé to help preserve surplus beans. They freeze-dried them.

discovery.text: During WWII, the U.S. military distributed instant coffee in ration packs. Soldiers called it 'a cup of Joe.'

twist.text: Instant coffee still dominates many markets. In the UK and Australia, it outsells ground coffee.

climax.text: New freeze-dry techniques have dramatically improved quality. Some specialty brands now make premium instant.

punchline.text: Born from surplus, fueled by war, still going strong.

quiz.question: Why was Nescafé originally created?
options: To help Brazil preserve surplus coffee beans

details.summary: Instant coffee was developed in the early 1900s but gained mass adoption when the US military adopted it for troops in both World Wars. Nescafe, launched by Nestle in 1938, became one of the world's most recognizable brands. Today, instant coffee still dominates global consumption by volume.
details.whyItMatters: Instant coffee democratized coffee globally by making it affordable and accessible everywhere. It remains the most consumed form of coffee worldwide despite specialty growth.
takeaways: Instant coffee gained mass adoption through military use in both World Wars
Nescafe launched in 1938 and became a global brand
Instant coffee still dominates global consumption by volume

faq.question: Who invented instant coffee?
faq.answer: Several inventors contributed. Satori Kato, a Japanese-American chemist, created an early version around 1901. George Washington, an English inventor living in Guatemala, commercialized it in 1910. Nestle's spray-drying process for Nescafe in 1938 made mass production practical.

faq.question: Why is instant coffee still so popular worldwide?
faq.answer: It is cheap, requires no equipment, and dissolves in hot water instantly. In many countries, it is the only affordable form of coffee. Global consumption of instant coffee exceeds specialty coffee many times over. In parts of Asia, Eastern Europe, and Africa, instant is the default.
